epistemic_contract.d4_actuality: Every model, computation, intervention, boundary condition, selection, and physical effect is actual D4.
epistemic_contract.d5_possibility: D5 contains represented or model-relative possible histories; its content does not act independently.
epistemic_contract.force_label_gate: F5-R remains a candidate history-selection law until it supplies a physical coupling, units, carrier or boundary source, conservation accounting, Lorentz behavior, range, and a distinct observable.

branches.statement: Represented futures influence present action through actual present models, signals, memories, institutions, and computations.
branches.mechanism: A D4 model token represents and reweights D5 alternatives, then ordinary present dynamics carries the effect into action.
branches.floor: F5-W0 is ordinary model-mediated anticipation and is compatible with F5-N.
branches.incremental_wager: F5-W+ is a distinct noetic operator that must add prediction beyond rich generic planning, control, and inference baselines.
branches.relation_to_F5_N: F5-N contains F5-W0 and contests only the F5-W+ increment or any additional interaction.
branches.strongest_rival: Salience, demand, reward, memory, expectancy, reactive control, or ordinary planning explains the measured change without a distinct D5-capacity variable.
branches.discriminator: Intervene on represented future content while holding relevant present means and confounds fixed; require incremental prediction beyond rich D4 baselines.
branches.kill: A fair-baseline null or the absence of an independently measurable future-content variable kills the distinct-capacity claim.
branches.survivor: Ordinary causal anticipation through present physical carriers.

branches.statement: No additional interaction couples to representation-as-such; selection, verification, correction, and revision service the D5 register.
branches.mechanism: Known physical interactions plus biological, cognitive, social, and verification mechanisms exhaust the observed effects.
branches.relation_to_F5_W: F5-N includes the F5-W0 present-model floor and denies an independently evidenced F5-W+ increment unless contact defeats the null.
branches.strongest_rival: F5-R predicts a preregistered residual dependence on later physical boundary data after ordinary channels are excluded.
branches.discriminator: Compare the frozen accepted-physics and control baseline with the F5-R history law on a held-out intervention.
branches.kill: A replicated force-specific residual with a defined coupling and observable kills this null in the tested range.
branches.survivor: Verification and revision remain necessary practices even if a new interaction is found.

branches.statement: An actual D4 history-selection law indexed by declared future boundary data and a D5 option functional may alter present transition probabilities.
branches.mechanism: A two-boundary or weighted-history law changes history weights; no possible future is treated as an agent and the future light cone is not treated as a source.
branches.strongest_rival: Standard quantum or classical dynamics, time-symmetric redescription, present-model control, common cause, selection bias, superdeterminism, or postselection predicts the same observations.
branches.discriminator: After an early outcome is irreversibly recorded, randomize a later physical boundary intervention without ordinary signalling or postselection and test the preregistered residual against the frozen null.
branches.kill: No exact law or observable fails admission; a preregistered null kills the promised parameter or range; observational equivalence yields UNDERDETERMINED rather than support.
branches.survivor: F5-W and F5-N remain viable; the option-preserving ethic remains a chosen orientation rather than physics.

The candidate law favors a declared option-preserving or ektropic class.
